recipes.name: Jeannie's Kickin' Fried Fish
ingredients_raw: 1 pound tilapia fillets, rinsed and patted dry
0.5 cup Italian seasoned bread crumbs (such as Progresso®)
1 teaspoon blackened seasoning (such as Old Bay®)
0.25 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, or to taste
0.25 teaspoon freshly ground sea salt, or to taste

steps.text: Beat egg with milk in a shallow bowl. In another shallow bowl, mix bread crumbs, roasted onion flakes, garlic, blackened seasoning, crushed red pepper flakes, black pepper, and salt together until combined.

Dip a tilapia fillet into egg mixture, then press gently into crumb mixture on both sides; set the coated fillet onto a plate. Repeat with remaining fillets; refrigerate the coated fillets for about 15 minutes to help set the crumbs.

Heat olive oil and butter in a cast-iron frying pan over medium heat. Lay fillets in the skillet, and pan-fry until golden brown on each side, about 3 minutes per side. The fish should be opaque and flaky underneath the coating. Remove and drain fillets on paper towels.

raw_recipe.headline: Jeannie's Kickin' Fried Fish
raw_recipe.description: These tilapia fillets, coated with crisp, light seasoned crumbs, pan-fry to a perfect golden brown in just a few minutes. The seasoning gives them a nice 'kick.'

video.description: In this video you'll see how to make a quick and easy fried fish. This version uses Cajun spices and seasoned breadcrumbs to make a crispy, flavorful crust. Fresh tilapia fillets hold up great here- but cod, halibut or even salmon would be equally delicious.

review.reviewBody: Instead of frying, I drizzled with butter, sprayed with pam and and baked in 400 degree. tasted awesome with less calories

A hit! I'm not the biggest fish fan and have nothing but praise for this easy recipe. I cooked this tonight using Panko crumbs to which I added Italian seasoning. Everything else was per the recipe. All of the spices blended beautifully, and even though I used liberal pinches of red pepper, it wasn't at all hot. It was just nicely seasoned, perfectly cooked and wonderfully crunchy. A definite winner, I'll make this spice blend part of my regular fish rotation. Thanks, crabbyjean! Update: I've made this many times now, and have found that letting the fish rest for an hour in the fridge makes the coating stick even better. I make a big batch of the coating mix using gluten free panko crumbs, Italian seasoning and all the spices so I always have it handy. It's great for coating chicken, too. BTW - I now love fish!

As written, the coating tends to flake off easily. try mixing the salt and pepper with 1/2 cup of flour and coat the fish in this, shake off excess before dipping in egg mixture, again let excess drip off, then coat with crumb mixture. Let rest for about 10 minutes before frying.

This was an awesome recipe and I used halibut. I added corn flakes crumbs and a little more red pepper flakes, put all of the ingredients in a large zip lock bag and rolled the batter so was quite fine. Really enjoyed it thanks!

jimmy

Today I tried this recipe and it was good. I did not have the roasted onions flakes, so I substituted with Mrs. Dash onion and herb seasoning, I also added 1tsp of parsley flakes. I the place the fish in the egg and milk mixture in a Tupperware bowl with a top and put in the refrigerator for 45 min. Then I put the dry ingredients in a plastic gallon size bag and put the fish in it and slightly shake the bag. I place the fish in a pan (spray pan with Pam) and drizzle the lemon and butter over it. Place pan in the refrigerator for 1 hour and place in oven for 35min on 325 or until golden brown. It was so tasty. This is going to be one of my favorite recipe for my favorite fish Tilapia.

Amazing! The changes I made are that I used haddock, used 3 teaspoons of mayo instead of an egg, added a 1/4 cup of flour to the pepper mix (to make it stick), used cornbread crumbs, and used onion powder and garlic powder instead of flakes and fresh garlic, but it still came out perfect! I'll definitely be making this again.

This recipe is great. I substituted flounder for the tilapia and omitted the crushed pepper flakes. Instead of frying, I baked it. I sprayed a cookie sheet large enough to hold the fish in one layer with cooking spray. Placed the breaded fillets on the sheet and lightly spray them with the cooking spray. Baked at 425 degrees for 20 minutes. It came out so good. Served with coleslaw, tartar sauce and roasted potatoes. We had enough left over to heat up and make four fish sandwiches the next day.

This is a great tasty way to pan fry a fish. I too kept the fish in the fridge a little longer than 15 mins. as others did, but didn't have time for a full hour, but it wasn't needed. Thirty mins worked fine for me. I had all the ingredients expect for the toasted onion, so I just used minced onion flakes. I will say that I did get some kicks in the taste but would prefer just a bit more. Next time, and there will be a next time, I'm going to put extra Old Bay in. Oh, and I never eat Talapia, so I used some Snapper that were thinner cuts than normal.

Strangely, I didn't have any eggs or milk on hand, so I just made the seasoned bread crumb mixture, coated fish on each side and fried in a pan as directed...squeezed a little lemon juice on it at the end, and it was fantastic! My new favorite. Easy and delicious!

Made this with cod fillets. Used Panko instead of bread crumbs and baked instead of fried - everything else as written. AWESOME!! Wonderful flavor. I did put the breaded fillets in the fridge for about an hour (just long enough to get the rest of my dinner together) before baking.

My mother only ever cooked fish in crumbs, but she used crushed Corn Flakes. I found it very good. I used ordinary bread crumbs as I found the rest of the ingredients seasoned enough. My Old Bay Mix (found the recipe here on AR) is highly spiced. I did find it hard to make the crumbs stick to the fish and I had to put the fillets back into the egg/milk and then the crumbs again. The first lot were well soaked and on the second try the crumbs stuck very well and the coating was quite thick.
Need more seasoning for my taste
Loved it
If you haven't made this your missing out on the Best fish I've ever eaten, I make it this way once a month and absolutely love it
Yum
I MADE THIS FISH AND THE WAY IT IS LISTED THIS IS VERY EASY AND MY FAMILY LOVED IT. THANK YOU
I followed the recipe and it was fantastic I will be making this again
It was good I made it just like the recipe using. Fresh self caught wonderful flaky white Lake Erie Walleye. It doesn’t get any better than this

I make it as written and my husband LOVES it! I have baked it instead of frying it to cut down on the fat by either drizzling a little EVOO or spraying with canola oil spray. It is a bit yummier fried, however.

I did not have roasted onion flakes, minced garlic, or ground sea salt. I ended up using granulated onion powder, garlic powder and some fine himalayan pink salt. I also used cod instead of tilapia and it was great. I can't wait to try it with tilapia. It makes a great fish sandwich. Quick and easy!
